title: Typed JSON schema subset with error paths
prompt:
Repair solve(payload), with schema and value. Every schema has type: object, array, string, integer,
number, boolean or null. Integers and numbers exclude booleans; integer also excludes float values
such as 1.0. An object schema may have properties (key -> schema), required (unique listed property
names), and additional (boolean, default true). An array may have items (schema for each element)
and min_items (nonnegative integer, default 0). A string may have min_length (nonnegative integer,
default 0), measured in Python Unicode code points. Other schema keywords do not occur. All schemas
are valid and required names occur in properties. Return [{"path": JSON_pointer,"code": error_code},...]
sorted by path then code. Codes are type, required, additional, min_items, min_length. A type mismatch
emits only type at that location; do not descend. Missing required fields get their prospective child
path. Forbidden extra fields get their own path and are not descended. Array length errors do not
prevent element validation. Root path is ""; escape '~' as '~0' and '/' as '~1' in object keys. Optional
absent properties are valid; unspecified array items accept anything. Depth is at most 10 and each
container has at most 30 members. Valid values return []. This is only the specified subset, not full JSON Schema.

Do not mutate the input. Use only Python's standard library.

Public examples:
- Input: `{"schema": {"type": "integer"}, "value": 7}`; output: `[]`.
- Input: `{"schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"x": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["x"]}, "value": {}}`; output: `[{"path": "/x", "code": "required"}]`.

files.public_tests.py:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
import copy
import json
import unittest
from solution import solve

CASES = json.loads('[{"name": "valid_integer", "input": {"schema": {"type": "integer"}, "value": 7}, "expected": []}, {"name": "missing", "input": {"schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"x": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["x"]}, "value": {}}, "expected": [{"path": "/x", "code": "required"}]}]')

class PublicExamples(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_examples(self):
        for item in CASES:
            with self.subTest(name=item["name"]):
                value = copy.deepcopy(item["input"])
                self.assertEqual(solve(value), item["expected"])
                self.assertEqual(value, item["input"], "solve must not mutate its input")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
